diagram_math_checks.detail: With M=A1 meet B1, U=A1 meet B0, V=A0 meet B1, both U and V lie below M from A0<=A1 and B0<=B1. Thus S=U join V<=M. The joins A0 join U<=A0 join M and V join B0<=M join B0 define the two outer quotient objects. These are exactly the statement quotients after substituting M,U,V.

The five named top/vertical maps are iL:M->A0 join M and iR:M->M join B0 (monomorphisms), qL:A0 join M->(A0 join M)/(A0 join U), p:M->M/S, and qR:M join B0->(M join B0)/(V join B0) (quotient epimorphisms). Bottom alpha:M/S->(A0 join M)/(A0 join U) and beta:M/S->(M join B0)/(V join B0) have the indicated orientations.

Step 1.1 and modularity [L1] give M meet (A0 join U)=(M meet A0) join U=V join U=S; step 1.2 gives M meet (V join B0)=V join (M meet B0)=S. The local second-isomorphism supplier proof 1.1 identifies such restricted quotient kernels via pullback. Its proof 2.1 and the image-of-biproduct definition of join show qL iL is epic since qL kills A0, and qR iR is epic since qR kills B0. Therefore alpha and beta are isomorphisms, as also established in the original steps 1.1 and 1.2.

The induced quotient maps are defined by alpha p=qL iL and beta p=qR iR, so these are precisely the two asserted commuting squares. The statement comparison has source the left quotient and target the right quotient and is beta alpha^{-1}. No additional exactness, lattice cover relation or commutativity is depicted. The rigorous original three-step proof remains unchanged and independent.
